findings.rationale: The model is prepared before cache-key inputs are reread. If the specification or a dependency changes between those operations, verification of the old model can be looked up or stored under a key describing newer bytes. Auto mode compounds this by recomputing the key after execution, allowing a stale verdict to poison the cache for the current source tree.

Approval creation independently loads the model, obtains the Git binding, hashes the specification, and later rereads it to render the approved artifact. A concurrent edit can therefore produce a record whose requirement set and spec digest describe one revision while its target digest describes another, even when the record is subsequently signed.

Migration plans retain replacement text from an earlier read, but commit only rechecks that each target is a regular file. It never verifies that the target still contains the planned source before renaming the replacement over it, so an edit made after planning is silently lost.

Domain generation creates directories and overwrites scaffold files one at a time without preflight, temporary files, or rollback. A failure on a later file returns an error after earlier files have already been changed; retrying repeats those writes against a partially generated tree and pre-existing files can be irreversibly clobbered.

Each approval file is read once to compute the combined digest and then reopened to parse the record. If it changes between reads, rendered or checked approval data comes from different bytes than the digest embedded in the document contract, yielding an internally inconsistent artifact.
